hydration_errors.homepage: [HYDRATION MISMATCH] Minified React error #418 — at Suspense

root_cause_analysis.why_fix_incomplete: The <Suspense> wrapper at L138 is still present in the React tree during hydration even when hydrated=false. Puppeteer prerender runs the full React lifecycle (incl. useEffect), so by capture time hydrated=true and the Suspense IS in the prerendered HTML. But React hydrateRoot requires <!--$?--> Suspense markers emitted by ReactDOM.renderToString — which Puppeteer doesn't produce. This causes #418 regardless of what is inside the Suspense.
root_cause_analysis.correct_fix: Move the Suspense boundary INSIDE the hydration gate: {hydrated && <Suspense fallback={null}><CmsAdminLayer /></Suspense>}. This removes the Suspense element entirely from the initial hydration pass. However, if Puppeteer captures AFTER effects (hydrated=true), prerendered HTML will have Suspense but client won't — still a mismatch. The ONLY complete fix is to NOT use hydrateRoot with Puppeteer-prerendered HTML, OR use suppressHydrationWarning on the wrapping element, OR move to ReactDOM.renderToString for prerendering.
root_cause_analysis.additional_note: The main Routes Suspense at App.js:73 also lacks Suspense markers (same root cause). If CmsAdminLayer fix is made correctly but this Suspense remains, #418 will still fire from the Routes Suspense.

rca_of_issue.problem: React #418 hydration mismatch on all pages despite CR-205 fix
rca_of_issue.root_cause: hydrateRoot requires Suspense HTML markers (<!--$?-->) from ReactDOM.renderToString. Puppeteer headless browser prerender does NOT emit these markers. Any Suspense boundary in the app will cause #418 when hydrateRoot runs against Puppeteer-generated HTML. The CR-205 fix moved CmsAdminLayer inside a hydrated gate but kept the <Suspense> wrapper present — the Suspense element itself is the mismatch trigger.
rca_of_issue.reproduction: Load any page fresh. Check console for [HYDRATION MISMATCH]. Error fires consistently on /, /pricing, /demo.
mitigation_options: Option A (safest): {hydrated && <Suspense fallback={null}><CmsAdminLayer /></Suspense>} AND ensure Puppeteer captures HTML before useEffect fires (configurable in prerender script via waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' instead of 'networkidle')
Option B: Add suppressHydrationWarning to the <div className='App'> wrapper
Option C: Switch prerender to use ReactDOM.renderToString instead of Puppeteer DOM capture
Option D: Remove hydrateRoot entirely — use createRoot for all cases (loses prerender SEO benefit)
